query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating to the surface of TC4 (Ti6Al4V) will improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties.
generation.material_initial_state: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) in its unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy state
generation.intervention: Application of a high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating to the surface of TC4
generation.conditions: Operating conditions involving high contact stress and extreme service environments
generation.structural_mediator: The HEA coating's unique microstructure, including a body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution and Laves phases, which contribute to its high strength and hardness
generation.mechanism: The HEA coating's high hardness and strength lead to improved wear resistance by reducing adhesive wear and abrasive wear, while its stable microstructure resists oxidation and corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved hardness and wear resistance of TC4, with a potential increase in its service lifetime and performance in high-contact-stress and extreme-service environments
generation.boundary: The operating conditions and environments in which the HEA-coated TC4 is expected to perform, including high temperatures, high pressures, and corrosive environments
generation.uncertainty: The optimal composition and microstructure of the HEA coating, as well as the potential effects of the coating on the underlying TC4 substrate

falsification_experiment.design: A controlled experiment involving the application of an HEA coating to TC4 and testing its wear resistance and hardness under various operating conditions
measurements: Hardness measurements using microindentation or nanoindentation techniques
Wear resistance measurements using ball-on-disk or pin-on-disk tribometry
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEA-coated TC4 exhibits no significant improvement in hardness and wear resistance compared to the untreated TC4, the hypothesis is falsified

The structural characteristics of TiC, TiB2, Ti2Ni, and matrix α-Ti composite phases were investigated. The results revealed an increase in the hardness of the coatings. Additionally, the coatings exhibited a lower wear rate of 47.8% and an average friction coefficient of 10.5% compared to TC4 substrate. The dominant wear mechanism was abrasive wear. High-entropy alloy (HEA) has been favored by many researchers because of its excellent properties, such as its superb specific strength [], good fatigue behavior [], wear and corrosion resistance [,,], super-conductivity [], and radiation tolerance [], etc. Due to these attractive properties, HEAs are promising candidates for technological applications in many fields, such as high-temperature applications [], nuclear energy industry [], space exploration, and storage of cryogens []. HEA was focused on high hardness for advanced industrial manufacturing. It is generally believed that materials with high hardness will have less slip and fewer dislocation vulnerabilities to resist cutting by force. Among these properties, wear is critical to the service lifetime of metallic parts with relatively moving contact surfaces, such as bearings and gears. Friction and wear during service may cause local deformation and failure of materials [,]. Therefore, developing wear-resistant metal alloys has been in high demand. Compared with traditional commercial alloys, HEA has excellent hardness, oxidation resistance, softening resistance and other properties, showing excellent wear resistance [,,,,

The wear rate is an important parameter to judge the wear resistance of materials. The wear rate of HEAs in the dry and lubrication conditions is shown in Figure 6b. To be more exact, the wear rate of the dry wear is higher than that of lubrication. The wear rates of the HEA in dry and lubrication conditions were approximately 17.2 × 10−5 mm3 N−1 m−1 and 12.4 × 10−5 mm3 N−1 m−1, respectively. According to a report by Haghdadi et al. [], the hardness and plasticity of the alloy under grinding conditions jointly determine material loss under medium and low load conditions. Although the hardness of AlCrFeNiV with a dual-phase BCC structure is very high, its plasticity is poor. When it is worn by the grinding ball with higher hardness, the material surface is prone to fracture, which means the increase in crushing degree, which is often accompanied by the generation of many fragments on the contact interface. They have sharp edges and a secondary grinding effect during sliding, increasing wear rates. In addition, the wear rate of the alloy in deionized water is significantly lower than that in dry conditions, probably due to lubrication.

In summary, a new equiatomic AlCrFeNiV alloy with dual-phase BCC was obtained through the combination of high-energy ball milling and a spark plasma sintering process. This strategy can be beneficial in the development of new materials that can be applied in cutting tools. The microstructure, microhardness and tribological properties were investigated in detail. The results are thus presented:(1)Microhardness reached 1076 ± 15 HV0.5, leading to a proper wear resistance. In addition, the wear behavior of AlCrFeNiV against Al2O3 ball under dry wear and lubrication conditions has been investigated. Compared with dry friction, the COF of AlCrFeNiV HEA with lubricant decreased significantly, whereas the decrease in the wear rate was not meditative.(2)The structure characterization indicates that two different kinds of body-centered cubic structures with different lattice parameters were formed in the AlCrFeNiV alloy, which is responsible for ultrahigh hardness.(3)The wear mechanism was found to be abrasive wear and oxidation wear by analyzing the worn surface.
